caption:
Schengen 90/180 rule: it is a rolling window, not a calendar year.

In any 180 days counting backwards from your entry date, your total days inside Schengen must stay under 90. It never resets on 1 January — it moves with you, daily.

The EU Entry/Exit System now records every crossing digitally. Miscounting is no longer a harmless error; it is a logged overstay that follows your future applications.

slides.headline: 90 DAYS — BUT WHICH 90?
slides.sub: It is a rolling window. It moves with you.
slides.note: It never resets on 1 January. Counting it wrong is now a recorded overstay.

slides.body: The window rolls. On any given day, look back 180 days and count how many you spent inside. That total is what matters.
slides.note: This is where accidental overstays come from — people counting calendar years.

slides.headline: TO COUNT IT YOURSELF
items: Add every day spent inside Schengen in that window

slides.headline: THE ENTRY/EXIT SYSTEM LOGS EVERY CROSSING.
slides.sub: Guesswork is no longer an option.

slides.headline: WHERE PEOPLE GET IT WRONG
items: Counting from the start of the year
Forgetting a short trip six months ago
Counting only full days, not entry and exit days
Assuming a new visa resets the count

slides.headline: WE COUNT IT FOR YOU.
checks: We plan the trip around the window
